clues: This small town lies in a valley in the west of South Africa. Fruit farms and grape vines fill the valley round it.
Most farms round here grow wheat and canola crops. Since a huge dam was built, this valley changed, and its small local climate now suits fruit trees and grape vines best.
A local farmer set up this town in 1843. The town took its name from that same man.
This is the only place in the whole country that dries persimmons. The town co-op does this one rare job.
A huge dam fills most of the valley floor by town. It is the biggest dam in its province, and it sends water to Cape Town.
